title: Global functions on affine inverse limits of qcqs spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their fppf sheaves and small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. All indexing sets are small in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale chart from a quasi-compact scheme; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback over every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, respectively the relative diagonal for a morphism, is quasi-compact. A morphism is affine if it is representable and its pullback over every affine scheme test has affine scheme source [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic spaces over $S$ with affine transition morphisms, and suppose the fppf sheaf $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ is an algebraic space with its specified projections. Write $A_i=\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal O_{X_i})$, with transition maps induced by the inverse-system morphisms. Pullback of functions induces an isomorphism of commutative rings $\varinjlim_i A_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Explicitly, every global function on $X$ comes from some $A_i$, and two elements of any $A_i$ with equal pullbacks to $X$ have equal images in $A_j$ for some $j\ge i$. The colimit is the ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 07SI (lemma-descend-section) in Situation 084R (situation-descent), specialized to the structure sheaf; no schematicity hypothesis on the stages.

proof.text: Choose $0\in I$ and work on the directed tail $J=\{i:i\ge0\}$. A compatible family on $J$ extends uniquely to $I$: for any $k$, choose $j\ge k,0$ and push the $j$-component to $k$; a common upper bound of two choices proves independence. This works for inverse-system points and for cocones on the direct system of rings, so neither the limit nor its colimit universal property changes. Choose a representable surjective etale map $U_0\to X_0$ with $U_0$ affine, using the finite-affine-atlas lemma (including its empty-space case). Set $R_0=U_0\times_{X_0}U_0$. The fibre-product lemma makes $R_0$ a scheme and both projections representable etale. The affine-scheme lemma makes $U_0$ qcqs; the qcqs-source-products lemma, applied over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ to $U_0,U_0,X_0$, makes $R_0$ qcqs. It does not require $X_0$ separated.

source.place: Tag 07SI (lemma-descend-section), specialized to the structure sheaf; Situation 084R (situation-descent)

proof.text: For $i\in J$ put $U_i=X_i\times_{X_0}U_0$ and $R_i=X_i\times_{X_0}R_0$. Associativity of sheaf fibre products identifies $R_i=U_i\times_{X_i}U_i$. Affine locality and base change make $U_i\to U_0$, $R_i\to R_0$, and every transition map affine; thus all $U_i,R_i$ are schemes, all $U_i$ are affine, and all $R_i$ are qcqs. Affine-scheme qcqs also applies to every $U_i$. The scheme-limit theorem supplies scheme limits $U=\varprojlim_J U_i$ and $R=\varprojlim_J R_i$. Every $U_i\to X_i$ is a representable surjective etale chart by base change of $U_0\to X_0$.

source.place: Tag 07SI (lemma-descend-section), specialized to the structure sheaf; Situation 084R (situation-descent)

proof.text: The specified fppf-sheaf limit identifies $U$ with $X\times_{X_0}U_0$: on any scheme $T$, a map to this fibre product is a compatible family $T\to X_i$ and one $T\to U_0$ over $X_0$, exactly a compatible family $T\to U_i$; the scheme-limit universal property identifies that family with $T\to U$. The same test identifies $R=X\times_{X_0}R_0=U\times_XU$, with its two projections. These bijections are natural in $T$ and hence are isomorphisms of sheaves. Base change of the atlas now makes $U\to X$ representable surjective etale. This argument uses only the assumed existence of $X$ and the scheme limits, not the parent lemma's assertion about algebraic-space limits.

source.place: Tag 07SI (lemma-descend-section), specialized to the structure sheaf; Situation 084R (situation-descent)

proof.text:
For a representable surjective etale scheme chart $V\to Y$ of an algebraic space and $W=V\times_YV$, the definition of the small etale structure sheaf gives
$\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=\operatorname{Eq}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\rightrightarrows\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W))$ as rings. Explicitly, a matching section on $V$ pulls back over each etale scheme $T\to Y$ to a matching section on the etale cover $T\times_YV\to T$. The sheaf axiom glues it uniquely to a section on $T$. Uniqueness gives compatibility for every arrow of the small site, hence a global section; it also gives injectivity of restriction to $V$. Addition and multiplication commute with these restrictions. Apply this to $(Y,V,W)=(X_i,U_i,R_i)$ and $(X,U,R)$. The resulting equalizers commute with all transition pullbacks, since both maps are pullback along the two projections and fibre-product associativity commutes with these projections.

source.place: Tag 07SI (lemma-descend-section), specialized to the structure sheaf; Situation 084R (situation-descent)

proof.text: Write $B_i=\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_{U_i})$, $C_i=\Gamma(R_i,\mathcal O_{R_i})$, and similarly $B,C$ at the scheme limits. Scheme section continuity applies to both systems: they are nonempty directed diagrams of qcqs schemes with affine transitions by step 2, with scheme limits by step 3. Thus $B=\varinjlim B_i$ and $C=\varinjlim C_i$, with representatives and eventual vanishing. For $a\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, let $b\in B$ be its restriction. Choose $b_i\in B_i$ representing $b$. The difference $d_i=s_i^*b_i-t_i^*b_i\in C_i$ pulls back to $s^*b-t^*b=0$. The eventual-vanishing clause for the $R_i$ system gives $j\ge i$ with $d_i|_{R_j}=0$. The image $b_j$ therefore belongs to the equalizer of step 4, giving $a_j\in A_j$. Its pullback to $X$ agrees with $a$ after restriction to $U$, so injectivity in step 4 proves equality. This proves representation of every global function.

source.place: Tag 07SI (lemma-descend-section), specialized to the structure sheaf; Situation 084R (situation-descent)

proof.text: If $a_i,a'_i\in A_i$ have equal pullbacks to $X$, their restrictions $b_i,b'_i\in B_i$ have difference with zero pullback to $U$. Scheme section continuity on the tail $j\ge i$ gives a stage $j\ge i$ at which that difference vanishes in $B_j$. Restriction $A_j\to B_j$ is injective by step 4, so the images of $a_i,a'_i$ in $A_j$ agree. For two representatives starting at distinct indices, first push them to a common upper bound. Thus equality of functions is exactly eventual equality of representatives. No transition map is assumed injective or surjective.

source.place: Tag 07SI (lemma-descend-section), specialized to the structure sheaf; Situation 084R (situation-descent)

proof.text: The representatives and equality criterion prove the ring-colimit universal property directly. Given a ring $D$ and compatible homomorphisms $h_i:A_i\to D$, define $h(a)=h_i(a_i)$ using a representative from step 5. Step 6 and a common upper bound show this is independent of the representative. Representing two functions at one common stage shows $h(a+a')=h(a)+h(a')$ and $h(aa')=h(a)h(a')$, and the representatives of $0,1$ show that $h$ is unital. Every function has a representative, so $h$ is the unique map extending the $h_i$. Hence the actual pullback cocone with apex $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is a colimit in commutative rings. Uniqueness of colimits identifies the canonical map in the statement with an isomorphism, and steps 5--6 are exactly its two explicit clauses. Cofinality from step 1 restores the original index set $I$.
